edges.description: Organisms that cross respiratory or enteric epithelial barriers enter blood and disseminate hematogenously.
Traumatic, post-neurosurgical, drain-associated, or shunt-associated organisms bypass bacteremia and directly inoculate CSF, ventricular hardware, or adjacent CNS tissue.
Bacteremic Gram-negative organisms traverse the blood-brain or blood-CSF barrier and reach cerebrospinal fluid.
Gram-negative bacteria multiply after entering the meningeal CSF space.
Gram-negative envelope products activate innate receptor signaling and recruit neutrophils into CSF.
Meningeal innate immune activation drives systemic fever.
Inflamed meninges and raised intracranial pressure produce headache.
Inflammation of the meningeal compartment produces clinical meningeal signs.
Pyogenic CSF inflammation and edema alter consciousness in acute Gram-negative meningitis.
The model follows pro-inflammatory mediator induction in CSF and brain tissue after Gram-negative K. pneumoniae meningitis.
edges.limitations: Experimental induction in adult Wistar rats does not reproduce species-specific human acquisition, neonatal E. coli disease, or post-neurosurgical device-associated inoculation.

nodes.description: Adult Wistar rats with induced K. pneumoniae meningitis are used to measure cytokines, chemokines, and memory impairment after Gram-negative meningeal infection.
Altered or fluctuating mental status occurs in healthcare-associated Gram-negative meningitis/ventriculitis.

evidence.reference_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa meningitis/ventriculitis in a UK tertiary referral hospital.
evidence.snippet: Pyrexia (75%), fluctuating mental status (50%) and headache (41%) were the most frequent presenting symptoms.

nodes.description: Fever is a frequent presentation in healthcare-associated adult Klebsiella and Pseudomonas branches of Gram-negative meningitis.

evidence.reference_title: Capsule and fimbriae modulate the invasion of Haemophilus influenzae in a human blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier model.
evidence.snippet: The H. influenzae capsule protects the bacteria against both phagocytosis and opsonization.

evidence.reference_title: Serotype O18 avian pathogenic and neonatal meningitis Escherichia coli strains employ similar pathogenic strategies for the onset of meningitis.
evidence.snippet: Using four representative APEC and NMEC strains that belong to serotype O18, we demonstrate that these strains survive in human serum similar to that of the prototypic NMEC strain E44, a derivative of RS218.

nodes.description: Replicating Gram-negative bacteria shed outer-membrane products, including lipopolysaccharide or lipooligosaccharide, into the cerebrospinal-fluid and subarachnoid compartments.

evidence.reference_title: Mesenchymal stem cells transplantation attenuates brain injury and enhances bacterial clearance in Escherichia coli meningitis in newborn rats.
evidence.snippet: Meningitis modeling induced robust proliferation of E. coli in the cerebrospinal fluid and increased mortality in rat pups, and MSC transplantation significantly reduced this bacterial growth and the mortality rate.

nodes.description: Gram-negative organisms cross into, or are directly introduced into, the cerebrospinal-fluid compartment.

evidence.reference_title: Meningococcal type IV pili recruit the polarity complex to cross the brain endothelium.
evidence.snippet: In Neisseria meningitidis, the causative agent of cerebrospinal meningitis, type IV pili-mediated adhesion to brain endothelial cells is required for bacteria to cross the blood-brain barrier.

evidence.reference_title: Capsule and fimbriae modulate the invasion of Haemophilus influenzae in a human blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier model.
evidence.snippet: To enter the central nervous system (CNS) the bacteria generally have to cross either the blood-brain barrier (BBB) or the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BSCFB).

nodes.description: Respiratory, enteric, maternal, traumatic, or neurosurgical exposure places meningitis-capable Gram-negative organisms at an epithelial surface or CNS device portal.

evidence.reference_title: 2017 Infectious Diseases Society of America's Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis.
evidence.snippet: Meningitis may not only be acquired in the community setting, but may be associated with a variety of invasive procedures or head trauma.

evidence.reference_title: Tumor necrosis factor in mediating experimental Haemophilus influenzae type B meningitis.
evidence.snippet: In CSF of rabbits with meningitis induced with Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) lipooligosaccharide (LOS), TNF activity was first detected 45 min after intracisternal (IC) injection of 20 ng Hib LOS and white blood cells (WBC) first appeared 75 min later.

evidence.reference_title: Tumor necrosis factor alpha/cachectin and interleukin 1 beta initiate meningeal inflammation.
evidence.snippet: These data provide evidence for a seminal role of TNF-alpha and IL-1 beta in the initial events of meningeal inflammation.

nodes.description: Clinical meningeal irritation is frequent in adult K. pneumoniae meningitis and reflects inflammation of the meningeal compartment.

nodes.description: Ceftriaxone or cefotaxime can treat third-generation-cephalosporin susceptible Gram-negative bacilli, while cefepime, ceftazidime, or meropenem are used for Pseudomonas species or resistant healthcare-associated Gram-negative rods according to susceptibility testing. Carbapenem-resistant healthcare-associated Gram-negative ventriculitis and meningitis can require polymyxin or other salvage regimens selected from isolate susceptibilities.

evidence.reference_title: 2017 Infectious Diseases Society of America's Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis.
evidence.snippet: For treatment of infection caused by gram-negative bacilli, therapy should be based on in vitro susceptibility testing with agents that achieve good CNS penetration (strong, moderate).

evidence.reference_title: 2017 Infectious Diseases Society of America's Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis.
evidence.snippet: For treatment of infection caused by Pseudomonas species, the recommended therapy is cefepime, ceftazidime, or meropenem (strong, moderate); recommended alternative antimicrobial agents are aztreonam or a fluoroquinolone with in vitro activity (strong, moderate).

evidence.reference_title: 2017 Infectious Diseases Society of America's Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis.
evidence.snippet: For patients with Acinetobacter ventriculomeningitis, empiric therapy should be initiated with meropenem. If carbapenem resistance is suspected, a combination of intravenous and intraventricular colistimethate sodium or polymyxin B is recommended [109].
